conventions.convention: Controls are real L2 almost-everywhere classes on a bounded Lebesgue-measurable domain; box bounds belong to L2 and are ordered almost everywhere. Equal bounds are allowed.
The elliptic state space carries the full H1 norm; the real bounded coercive bilinear form need not be symmetric. The regularization parameter α is strictly positive.
The adjoint satisfies a(v,p)=(Ju−u_d,Jv); B*p is represented in the real control inner product. The reduced gradient has the positive sign B*p+αq.
Countable Choice is assumed for Hilbert completeness, Riesz representation and the minimizing-sequence argument; the weak-subsequence lemma concerns separable real Hilbert spaces.

Cell averaging preserves the admissible box only when both bounds are constant on each control cell. Projection onto the cellwise box clips cell averages, rather than averaging a pointwise-clipped function.
The projected-gradient loop targets the exact continuous PDE objective restricted to Q_h. Its two backends must return in finite time with exact valid outputs or failure.

The parabolic horizon is positive, V is separable, the adjoint has terminal value zero, and state variations have initial value zero. Time-dependent comparison maps require operator-norm C1 regularity.

The SQP wrapper certifies the intended active linear system using unchanged exactly representable stored data. A nonlinear next-point KKT residual, feasibility and multiplier signs require separate checks.

load_bearing.statement: Under the defined elliptic setting and Countable Choice, the reduced gradient is B*p(q)+αq, its Hessian is S*S+αI, its gradient is Lipschitz with constant ||S||²+α, and the objective is α-strongly convex.
Under Countable Choice and the defined elliptic setting, each q has a unique state and transposed-form adjoint, with bounds ||u(q)||_V≤||f+Bq||/β and ||p(q)||_V≤||J|| ||Ju(q)−u_d||/β.
Under Countable Choice and the defined elliptic setting, the objective has a unique minimizer q* in Q_ad, characterized equivalently by (B*p(q*)+αq*,v−q*)≥0 for every v in Q_ad.

For the stated conforming perturbed state and transposed adjoint problems, the complete first-Strang bounds give state error at most ε_u, adjoint error at most ε_p, and gradient error at most ||B|| ε_p; the adjoint load defect includes ||J||² ε_u.
Cell averaging is the L2 orthogonal projection onto cellwise constants and satisfies ||q−Π_hq||_L2≤Ch|q|_H1 on the stated matching affine simplicial meshes; it preserves cellwise-constant box bounds.
On the stated finite matching affine control mesh with cellwise-constant ordered bounds, clipping each cell average gives the unique L2 projection onto Q_h, and this projection is nonexpansive.
Assume Countable Choice. Every bounded sequence in a separable real Hilbert space has a weakly convergent subsequence.

With the stated admissible finite-return routines, the algorithm terminates within N iterations. A certified return has exact projected-gradient residual at most ρ≤τ and distance to the restricted exact-PDE optimum at most (L_h/α)ρ.

concerns.concern: The Statement never specifies the fixed source f from the cited control-problem definition. Verification 1.1 uses a(u*,v)=(q*,v), which identifies the stated u* as the state only for f=0. The intended zero source is immediately inferable from the displayed differential equation, but should be explicitly included among the example's data.

Fact F2 says: 'For α>0, an admissible control satisfying the adjoint box projection formula is the unique minimizer', citing cor-linear-elliptic-control-projection-formula. That corollary states the formula for the already identified minimizer, rather than its converse. Verification 2.1 can close the converse immediately using the projection variational inequality and thm-linear-elliptic-control-existence-and-variational-inequality, but F2 states its cited source more strongly than written.

seams_checked.note: The lower/upper box gradient signs agree with g_i≤0 and nonnegative multipliers. The finite active-system certificate is explicitly distinguished from full KKT feasibility, signs and complementarity; no constraint-qualification converse is imported.

Cell averaging uses matching affine nondegenerate simplices, null facets, affine weak pullback and reference Poincaré–Wirtinger. Determinants cancel in the cell estimate; box preservation retains cellwise-constant bounds.
The cited exact proximal-gradient procedure supplies context. This batch separately defines its inexact-gradient loop and proves its residual certificate, without importing exact-call FISTA rates.

The rate discussions preserve conformity, primal approximation, matching dual approximation and actual H2 regularity. The O(h²) control theorem explicitly assumes the complete uniform L2 state/adjoint estimate rather than deriving it from an O(h) energy estimate alone.

The parabolic result supplies T>0, separable V and the measurable uniformly bounded/coercive form hypotheses. Time reversal uses the transposed form; integration by parts retains both traces. The comparison-map derivative includes P_h'u.

The gradient certificate uses the first Strang estimate for conforming primal and transposed problems, retaining discrete coercivity, approximation, form and load defects, including the state-error contribution to the adjoint load.

The connection is contextual: the elliptic control derivative is proved locally. Its positive load-derivative sign and transposed adjoint agree with the parameterized sensitivity interface; no general derivative-data defect bound or additional rate is imported.

The wrapper uses the QR-returned step and intended-data residual certificate. The nonlinear local convergence branch retains identified active set, LICQ, strict complementarity, reduced curvature, locally Lipschitz Jacobian and a sufficiently close start; it is explicitly separate from finite-precision status.
